question: When a language model is fine-tuned on random or flipped labels to suppress a task, does the resulting behavioral forgetting generalize to held-out instances and other tasks, what predicts that generalization, and is the task information actually erased?

key_findings.claim: Random-label fine-tuning reliably changes training-example behavior but has sharply task-dependent generalization to held-out examples.
key_findings.evidence: Across 21 binarized multiple-choice tasks, Llama-2-7B often remains above chance after the forgetting phase; commonsense and scientific QA are comparatively resilient, whereas several entailment and linguistic tasks approach chance.

key_findings.claim: The evaluation task predicts the cross-task forgetting outcome more strongly than the task supplying randomized labels.
key_findings.evidence: The cross-task matrix clusters mainly by evaluation columns: some capabilities remain robust after random-label training on many other tasks, and some tasks are suppressed more by unrelated randomized data than by their own data.

key_findings.claim: Task difficulty is not a useful predictor, while lower initial answer confidence and lower representation variance are weak task-level predictors of greater forgetting.
key_findings.evidence: ARC-Easy is less forgettable than harder ARC-Challenge; task-level plots relate forget ratio to confidence and to the trace of the hidden-state covariance. The same quantities do not predict which individual examples will be forgotten.

key_findings.claim: Learning and forgetting order are modestly anticorrelated.
key_findings.evidence: After excluding examples never crossing the 0.6 confidence thresholds, examples learned earlier tend to be forgotten later across the plotted tasks, although the relationship is weak.

key_findings.claim: Behavioral suppression is shallow rather than verified information removal.
key_findings.evidence: Linear probes trained on fifth-from-last-layer representations retain broadly comparable correct-versus-incorrect classification accuracy before and after random-label forgetting, even when prompt-level task accuracy falls.

key_findings.claim: The reported robustness checks support recurrence of the qualitative pattern, not scale-independent or method-independent unlearning.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix varies label corruption, dataset size, and models from GPT-2-124M through GPT-J-6B and Llama-2-7B, but all variants remain full fine-tuning on binary-choice tasks and use the same behavioral metric family.

method.core_idea: Fine-tune a pretrained model on a task, then fine-tune the same examples with labels resampled uniformly each epoch, measuring how much held-out and cross-task accuracy returns toward chance.
method.mechanism: Define a chance-adjusted forget gap and forget ratio; sweep 21 binary-choice datasets; compare same-task and all-pairs cross-task forgetting; correlate task-level forgetting with accuracy, relative answer confidence, and hidden-state covariance trace; compare per-example learning/forgetting order; finally test latent recoverability with regularized linear probes.
assumptions: Chance-level multiple-choice accuracy is an adequate behavioral proxy for forgetting.
Binarizing heterogeneous benchmarks preserves the capability whose removal matters.
Random-label and flipped-label fine-tuning are informative models of practical unlearning.
Linear decodability is evidence that task-relevant information remains, although failure to decode would not prove erasure.
Task-level correlations over 21 datasets are stable enough to motivate predictors despite the small effective sample size.

techniques.role: Creates a simple suppression intervention by repeatedly training uniformly randomized answers.
Normalizes post-intervention accuracy by supervised accuracy and the binary random baseline.
Separates the effect of the intervention dataset from susceptibility of the evaluation capability.
Uses covariance-trace breadth of hidden states as a label-free task-level predictor.
Tests whether behaviorally inaccessible answers remain linearly recoverable from intermediate states.

evaluations.setting: Llama-2-7B on 21 binarized commonsense, reading, math, toxicity, entailment, and language-understanding tasks, up to 1,000 examples each.
evaluations.metric: Held-out accuracy, forget gap, and forget ratio.
evaluations.result: Forgetting ranges from near-chance behavior to little loss of fine-tuned accuracy, with commonsense-oriented tasks generally more resistant.
evaluations.baseline: Pretrained, supervised-fine-tuned, and binary chance accuracy.

evaluations.setting: All-pairs cross-task random-label fine-tuning and evaluation.
evaluations.result: Susceptibility depends mainly on the evaluated task; unrelated random-label data can suppress some tasks more than their own corrupted labels.

evaluations.setting: 100 versus 1,000 forgetting examples; random versus flipped labels; GPT-2-124M, GPT-J-6B, and Llama-2-7B.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative ordering and forget ratios across tasks.
evaluations.result: The broad task-dependent ordering recurs, although individual values and attainable fine-tuned accuracy vary.

evaluations.setting: Regularized linear probes on intermediate representations after pretraining, task fine-tuning, and random-label forgetting.
evaluations.metric: Held-out probe accuracy for classifying candidate answers as correct or incorrect.
evaluations.result: Probe effectiveness changes little after behavioral forgetting.
evaluations.baseline: Probes on pretrained and supervised-fine-tuned representations.

limitations: Author-stated: the proposed predictors work at task level but not at individual-example level.
Reviewer inference: 21 heterogeneous tasks provide few independent units for correlation claims, and no uncertainty intervals or held-out predictor validation are reported.
Reviewer inference: binary multiple-choice accuracy omits generative elicitation, paraphrases, adversarial prompting, privacy leakage, and relearning attacks.
Reviewer inference: the intervention is suppression by ordinary full fine-tuning, not deletion of a specified pretraining contribution or comparison with retraining without that data.
Reviewer inference: the largest evaluated model is 7B and all models are older base LMs, limiting conclusions about current instruction-tuned or reasoning models.
failure_modes: A model appears forgotten under the fixed prompt but reveals the capability under another format or an extraction attack.
Training on corrupted labels produces broad capability damage rather than targeted removal.
Chance accuracy hides systematic but label-permuted knowledge.
Linear probes recover an evaluation artifact rather than the capability, or nonlinear information remains when a linear probe fails.
A task-level predictor learned from benchmark identities fails on a new capability distribution.
reusable_insights: Unlearning evaluation should distinguish intervention-side coverage from evaluation-side susceptibility with an explicit cross-task matrix.
Behavioral failure, latent recoverability, adversarial elicitation, and relearning robustness are separate validation layers.
A label-free representation-spread statistic is a useful candidate triage signal, but it needs prospective validation on unseen tasks.
Learning and forgetting trajectories provide more mechanistic information than a single endpoint score.
open_questions: Can a predictor trained on representation geometry forecast forgetting for genuinely unseen tasks, models, and intervention methods?
Which causal representation changes distinguish genuine capability removal from output-layer suppression?
Do the same task-susceptibility patterns hold under RMU, NPO, retain-set regularization, or exact retraining baselines?
How quickly do the supposedly forgotten capabilities return under benign downstream fine-tuning?
Can generative, adversarial, and privacy-focused tests be combined without collapsing distinct unlearning goals into one score?

competitive_landscape.title: Eight Methods to Evaluate Robust Unlearning in LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: Lynch et al. audit extraction, latent knowledge, relearning, and collateral effects for a fact-unlearned model; this paper instead maps held-out and cross-task generalization of skill suppression over many tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: MUSE evaluates memorization, privacy, utility, scalability, and sequential requests across eight algorithms; this paper isolates task-level generalization and latent linear recoverability for random-label fine-tuning.

competitive_landscape.title: Machine Unlearning of Pre-trained Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Yao et al. compare seven efficient unlearning algorithms and retain-distribution training; this study uses one deliberately simple intervention to expose variability in generalization across capabilities.

competitive_landscape.title: Invariance Makes LLM Unlearning Resilient Even to Unanticipated Downstream Fine-Tuning
competitive_landscape.difference: ILU explicitly regularizes invariance to improve robustness under unseen downstream fine-tuning, addressing a stronger persistence criterion than endpoint random-label suppression.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The work reveals extreme cross-task variability in the generalization of skill forgetting, identifies task-level correlates, and shows that successful behavioral forgetting remains linearly decodable.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The 21-task same- and cross-task matrices, trajectory analysis, and probes directly support those descriptive claims under the chosen intervention.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The distinctive contribution is the evaluation-side susceptibility map and its shallow-forgetting diagnosis, not a new unlearning algorithm. Later robust-unlearning suites cover a broader threat model, so the result is best treated as a mechanistic warning and experimental design pattern.

reviewer_notes: Read all 18 pages, including fine-tuning details and model/method/data-size appendices. Competitive records were checked at primary arXiv or OpenReview pages on 2026-08-23; causal language is avoided because the predictors are correlational.
